content: Initial plan for daily-driver: SessionStart recall hook (fail-soft, stdlib-only, REST-based, domain from cwd), /engram skill with suggestion-first checkpoint + explicit search/store/status subcommands, four MCP prompts (start_day/switch_project/end_session/weekly_review), project-status v1 as tag convention (type:project-status, propose->confirm->record, no schema), conventions + install guide in docs/workflows.md and integrations/claude-code/. Verification is demonstration-based in-cycle with the week-long adoption trial running in parallel with Phase 11. Plan at docs/phases/daily-driver.md.

The daily-driver direction is strong, but the plan needs changes at the data and workflow boundaries before implementation.

1. Make project-status records full snapshots, not deltas. The plan currently says checkpoint drafts a "project-status delta" while the newest `type:project-status` memory is treated as canonical status. A latest delta is not a usable status document. Define a compact versioned Markdown/JSON contract (at minimum: project/domain, goal, current state, recent progress, blockers/open questions, next actions, updated_at/evidence) and require each confirmed `type:project-status` write to contain the complete current snapshot. The separate checkpoint can record the session delta/evidence.

2. Provide deterministic scoped retrieval instead of approximating "latest" through semantic search. `POST /api/search/` ranks by RRF relevance, not recency, and cannot guarantee that the latest status or latest domain memories are in its candidate pool. The current REST list surface also lacks tag filters. Add the smallest backend read surface needed (for example, tag/source/limit filtering on `GET /api/memories/`, or a dedicated project-context endpoint) so the hook can fetch the newest status and recent scoped memories deterministically. Keep it read-only and tested. Do not client-filter an unscoped list or treat a semantic query as chronological retrieval.

3. Specify and test the actual Claude Code hook contract. The global `SessionStart` command receives JSON on stdin; derive the project from the input `cwd`, not an assumed process cwd. Define the `.engram` marker format, validation/normalization, and precedence (`ENGRAM_DOMAIN` > marker > repository/directory slug). Document whether the hook runs on startup/resume/clear/compact and avoid duplicate/noisy injection where appropriate. Tests should cover malformed stdin, missing cwd, HTTP/auth errors, invalid JSON, timeouts, empty results, output-size capping, and successful context output. Keep fail-soft behavior and explicit per-request/total timeout budgets.

4. Make the four MCP prompts executable with available data. `start_day` and `weekly_review` cannot reliably aggregate across domains because current MCP tools do not enumerate all project domains (`get_stats` exposes only top tags and `list_recent_memories` is globally limited). Either add a minimal `list_domains`/project-discovery read tool, or make an explicit domain list a required prompt argument until Phase 11 provides a project registry. Define prompt arguments and tool sequence for all four prompts, especially `switch_project` and `end_session`, and unit-test that they reference only tools/arguments that actually exist.

5. Clarify the capture trigger. A `/engram checkpoint` skill is user-invoked; it is not automatic "session-end capture." For v1, it is acceptable—and likely less intrusive—to call this a manual suggestion-first checkpoint. If a hook reminds the user, it must be non-writing, low-noise, and explicitly designed; a `SessionEnd` hook cannot conduct an interactive confirmation after the session has terminated. Ensure the Summary, Scope, docs, and success criteria describe the same trigger.

6. Preserve the real adoption criterion in full-roadmap mode. A single demonstration proves mechanics, not that the daily driver "sticks." It is fine for Phase 11 identity work to proceed during the trial, but the watcher must not use nonexistent daily-driver evidence at the Phase 12 project-model decision. Add a tracked adoption log/feedback mechanism and a gate before Phase 12: either obtain the user's confirmation after meaningful use across at least two projects, or explicitly record that evidence is insufficient and defer the project-model decision. Do not silently replace the roadmap's one-week criterion with one demo.

7. Expand installation success criteria to cover a second repository end to end: merge (do not overwrite) global Claude settings, install/symlink the skill and hook, configure the Engram MCP HTTP server for that repository or user scope, resolve the expected domain, and verify recall/search there. This is important because the current MCP registration is only known to work in the Engram project.

Keep the phase focused: these changes do not require identity files, hard workspaces, per-agent auth, or automatic writes. They make the v1 convention internally coherent and verifiable before it becomes ambient across projects.

All 7 requests addressed; plan rewritten (docs/phases/daily-driver.md) with a new "Data contracts" section, plus matching roadmap edits.

1. Full snapshots: type:project-status content is now a complete self-contained Markdown status document with a fixed section contract (Goal/State/Recent/Blockers/Next/Updated+Evidence); every confirmed write carries the whole snapshot (drafting reads the previous one and carries forward unchanged sections). Checkpoints hold session deltas and never stand in for status.

2. Deterministic retrieval: new scope item 1 adds tags/source/limit query params to GET /api/memories/ passed to memory_service.list_recent (created-at ordered; service already supports these filters — only the HTTP surface is new). Hook and skill use list filters for latest-status/recents; RRF search is relevance-only. Read-only, bounded (limit<=100, <=10 tags), unit-tested.

3. Hook contract specified: stdin JSON is the source of cwd (never process cwd); domain precedence ENGRAM_DOMAIN > .engram marker (one line, domain=<slug>) > directory slug, with [a-z0-9-] normalization and fallback; runs on startup and clear, silent on resume and compact (duplicate-injection avoidance); <=4KB output cap; 1.5s/request, 3s total, no retries; fail-soft on malformed stdin, missing cwd, HTTP/auth errors, invalid JSON, timeouts, empty results. tests/test_recall_hook.py enumerates exactly these cases.

4. Prompts executable: new list_domains MCP tool (distinct domain:* tags with counts, same aggregation style as /api/tags/) so start_day and weekly_review enumerate projects deterministically; all four prompts now specify arguments and exact tool sequences (switch_project(domain) and end_session(domain) require the arg); tests assert referenced tool names exist on the server.

5. Capture trigger clarified everywhere: it is a manual, user-invoked suggestion-first checkpoint (/engram checkpoint or end_session prompt); no automatic session-end write, no hook conducts confirmation; Summary, Scope, out-of-scope, roadmap Phase 10 wording all now say the same thing.

6. Adoption gate: new docs/adoption-log.md deliverable with dated per-project usage entries; roadmap Phase 12 decision checkpoint now carries an explicit gate — human confirmation of meaningful use across >=2 projects recorded in the log, or an explicit "insufficient evidence — decision deferred" entry. The one-week criterion is tracked, not replaced; in-cycle demo is labeled mechanics-only.

7. Second-repo criterion: success criterion 5 requires end-to-end install in a second real repository following the README verbatim — merging (not overwriting) ~/.claude/settings.json hooks, skill install, user/repo-scope MCP registration, domain resolution, and working recall + scoped search there, transcribed in the submission.

The revised plan addresses the seven major requests and is close to approval. Three narrow contract gaps remain:

1. Make the hook's "latest 5 non-status memories" retrieval implementable. The proposed REST filter supports only ALL-of `tags`; `tags=domain:<d>` can return status snapshots, and there is no negative tag filter. Choose and document one exact behavior: either fetch recent checkpoints specifically with `tags=domain:<d>,type:checkpoint`, add a bounded `exclude_tags=type:project-status` filter, or fetch a sufficiently bounded scoped list and explicitly client-filter (with clear completeness semantics). The plan and tests must match. Do not claim the API can directly return non-status records when it cannot.

2. Make `weekly_review(domains, days)` implementable with real time filtering. The stated sequence uses `list_recent_memories`, but that MCP tool currently has no `after`/`before` argument, so `days=7` cannot be enforced and a global limit can omit in-window checkpoints. Add an `after` filter to the relevant service/MCP read path (and tests), or remove `days` and state the bounded semantics honestly. Prefer adding an optional `after` argument so the prompt can calculate the cutoff and fetch each domain's checkpoints deterministically. Update the Files and Success Criteria for this addition.

3. Define repository-root discovery for domain resolution. The marker is said to live at the repo root, but stdin `cwd` may be a subdirectory. Specify a bounded upward walk from the hook payload's cwd for `.engram`, stopping at the filesystem root; if no marker exists, use the nearest Git root directory name when available, otherwise the cwd basename. Keep the existing precedence and normalization. Add subdirectory/marker/root cases to hook tests. This prevents one repository from acquiring different domains depending on where Claude Code starts.

Everything else in round 2 is accepted, including the full-snapshot contract, deterministic status endpoint, prompt discovery tool, manual checkpoint trigger, adoption gate, and second-repository verification.

All 3 contract gaps closed in docs/phases/daily-driver.md:

1. Non-status retrieval is now exact: added `exclude_tags` (comma, ANY-of exclusion, <=5 tags, `.exclude(tags__contains=[t])` per tag) to GET /api/memories/ and memory_service.list_recent. The hook's two fetches are specified verbatim: `tags=domain:<d>,type:project-status&limit=1` for status and `tags=domain:<d>&exclude_tags=type:project-status&limit=5` for recents — the API returns non-status records itself; no client filtering, no completeness caveats. Files + criteria updated.

2. weekly_review time filtering is real: new optional `after` (ISO date) argument on the list_recent_memories MCP tool backed by a created_at >= after filter in memory_service.list_recent; the prompt computes the cutoff from `days` and fetches per-domain checkpoints deterministically. Both service filter and tool argument unit-tested; Files and Success Criteria updated accordingly.

3. Repo-root discovery defined: bounded upward walk (<=20 levels, stop at filesystem root) from the stdin payload's cwd for the `.engram` marker; if absent, nearest ancestor containing `.git` supplies its directory name; else cwd basename. Precedence and [a-z0-9-] normalization unchanged. Hook tests now include subdirectory resolution (marker via walk, git-root fallback, basename fallback), so one repo yields one domain regardless of where the session starts.

Approved. The final plan has coherent full-snapshot and checkpoint contracts, deterministic scoped/status/non-status retrieval, implementable cross-project and time-bounded MCP prompts, a well-specified fail-soft SessionStart hook, manual confirmation-only writes, stable repository domain resolution, second-repository verification, and a genuine adoption gate before the Phase 12 project-model decision.
